g.text: FIGURE 4: HIGHER-ORDER LINEAR ODES & COMPLEMENTARY FUNCTION ARCHITECTURE
Differential Operator D, Auxiliary Equation f(m) = 0, The 4 Root Regimes & Wronskian Linear Independence Metric
CANONICAL n-th ORDER LINEAR CONSTANT COEFFICIENT ODE
dⁿy/dxⁿ + a₁ dⁿ⁻¹y/dxⁿ⁻¹ + ... + aₙ y = X(x)
Differential Operator notation: Let D = d/dx, D² = d²/dx², ..., Dⁿ = dⁿ/dxⁿ.
f(D) y = X(x) where f(D) = Dⁿ + a₁ Dⁿ⁻¹ + ... + aₙ
• Complementary Function (CF): General solution of homogeneous ODE: f(D) y = 0.
• Particular Integral (PI): Any particular solution of non-homogeneous equation: f(D) y = X.
Trial solution y = e^(mx) substituted into f(D) y = 0 yields algebraic polynomial:
Roots m₁, m₂, ..., mₙ completely govern the functional form of the CF.
CASE 1: REAL AND DISTINCT ROOTS (m₁ ≠ m₂ ≠ ... ≠ mₙ)
CF = c₁ e^(m₁ x) + c₂ e^(m₂ x) + ... + cₙ e^(mₙ x)
Example: m = 2, -3 ⟹ CF = c₁ e^(2x) + c₂ e^(-3x).
CASE 2: REAL AND REPEATED ROOTS (m₁ = m₂ = ... = m_k = m)
CF = (c₁ + c₂ x + c₃ x² + ... + c_k x^(k-1)) e^(m x)
Example: m = 3, 3, 3 ⟹ CF = (c₁ + c₂ x + c₃ x²) e^(3x).
CASE 3: COMPLEX CONJUGATE PAIR (m = α ± iβ)
CF = e^(α x) [ c₁ cos(β x) + c₂ sin(β x) ]
Purely imaginary (α = 0): m = ±iβ ⟹ CF = c₁ cos(β x) + c₂ sin(β x) (Harmonic oscillator!).
CASE 4: REPEATED COMPLEX ROOTS (m = α ± iβ repeated k times)
CF = e^(α x) [ (c₁ + c₂ x) cos(β x) + (c₃ + c₄ x) sin(β x) ]
Example: (D² + 1)² y = 0 ⟹ m = ±i, ±i ⟹ CF = (c₁ + c₂ x) cos x + (c₃ + c₄ x) sin x.
For two differentiable functions y₁(x) and y₂(x):
W(y₁, y₂) = | y₁ y₂ | = y₁ y₂' - y₂ y₁'
• W(x) ≠ 0 at any point in domain ⟺ y₁, y₂ are LINEARLY INDEPENDENT.
• W(x) ≡ 0 everywhere in domain ⟺ y₁, y₂ are LINEARLY DEPENDENT (y₁ = k y₂).
For the 2nd order linear ODE: y'' + P(x) y' + Q(x) y = 0:
Remarkable Property: If W is zero at ONE point, it is identically ZERO everywhere!
If one non-zero solution y₁(x) is known, second independent solution y₂(x) is:
y₂(x) = y₁(x) · ∫ [ e^( - ∫ P dx ) / (y₁)² ] dx
4. BENCHMARK CF EXAM PROBLEMS & ROOT DECOUPLING ARSENAL
y = c₁ e^(2x) + c₂ e^(-2x) + c₃ cos(2x) + c₄ sin(2x)
y = C₁ cosh(2x) + C₂ sinh(2x) + c₃ cos(2x) + c₄ sin(2x)
Notice: 4 essential arbitrary constants match the 4th order ODE!
Step 3: Combine exponential shift and linear polynomials:
y = e^(2x) [ (c₁ + c₂ x) cos(3x) + (c₃ + c₄ x) sin(3x) ]
Do NOT write (c₁ + c₂x) e^(2x) cos(3x) + c₃ sin(3x);
BOTH sine and cosine terms must have the multiplying factor (c + dx)!
y = e^(√3 x) [ c₁ cos x + c₂ sin x ]
+ e^(-√3 x) [ c₅ cos x + c₆ sin x ]
Whenever m⁶ = -a⁶ appears, the roots always form a symmetric regular hexagon on the complex plane centered at origin with radius a!
